full_judgment:
2. The petitioner as plaintiff filed Other Class Suit No. 54 of 2001 before the Court of Assistant Judge, Thrash, and Sirajganj for declaration of title of 2.27 acres of land and further declaration that the Deed No. 8999 dated 24.11.1969 of Naogaon Sub-Registry office was forged collusive not acted upon and not binding upon the plaintiff. The case of the plaintiff, inter alia, was that 3.06 acres land of C.S. Plot No. 403 in C.S. Khatian No. 41 under Sree Krishnapur Mouza originally belonged to Brindaban Goshwami and the same was recorded in his name as pond; that Brindahan Goshwami was a Brahman Priest and he used to live at another village namely Handial under Chatmohar Police Station of Palma District and possessed the same through a caretaker named Sree Badal; that in addition said Brindaban Goshwami occasionally used to live at the home constructed in the eastern part of the pond for maintaining the property and the S.A. Khatian No. 61 was prepared in his name correctly in respect of said property; that Brindaban Goshwami had no child and due to inconvenience in managing the pond because of shortage of manpower he kept .38 acre land in eastern part of the pond whereupon a but was built under his own management and sold the remaining 2.68 acres to the plaintiff by way of registered sale deed No. 11727 dated 19.09.1979 corresponding to 2nd Aswin, 1386 B.S.; that after purchase, the plaintiff had been possessing the purchased land and in R.S. record entered his name in R.S. Khatian No. 397 and converted plot No. 473 but when the plaintiff submitted the original sale deed to the Tahshilder, the concerned Tahshilder lost it; that the plaintiff obtained the finally published corrected R.S. record; that in the meantime the defendant in collusion with the custodians of R.S. record volume could enter his name. in printed parcha in place of plaintiffs name in R.S. Khatian No. 397 by eliminating the plaintiff's name which is illegal; that for extension of periphery of Sree Krishnapur Hat as per demand by the committee, the plaintiff transferred .41 acre out of the suit land in favour of Hat Committee and the plaintiff had been possessing remaining 2.27 acres of land peacefully by rearing fish and planting different trees in the southern part of the suit land; that while the plaintiff was possessing the remaining 2.27 acres of land, all of a sudden he received notice of Miscellaneous Case No. 80 of 2001 of the office of Assistant Commissioner (Land) Tarash and on 29.04.2001 searched the office and came to know about the existence of deed No. 8999 dated 24.11.1969 of Naogaon Sub-Registry Office in respect of Suit land which is a product of collusive acts. Hence, he filed the suit. 

 3. The defendant contested the suit, by filing written statement denying the material facts and allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that Brindaban Goshwami sold 1.90 acres of land from Plot No. 403 by way of registered deed of sale No. 8999 dated 24.11.1969 and accordingly his name was recorded in R.S. Khatian No. 397; that 2.68 acres out of 3.06 in C.S. and R.S. Plot No. 403 was recorded in R.S. Plot No. 473 and remaining .38 acre was recorded in R.S. Plot No. 474 and the defendant purchased .38 acre of land from Badal Chandra Bashak but got entire 3.06 acres of land; that the defendant transferred .40 acre of land from Northern part in favour of Sree Krishnapur hat committee and the defendant is possessing remaining 2.66 acres of land; that the original owner of the land died in the year 1972-73 and the plaintiff has no right title and possession but he filed this suit, with created documents and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 7. Mr. A. M. Aminuddin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that both the Courts below having seen of the original deed dated 24.11.1969 (Ext. 'ka') which had been filed by the defendant, came to a finding that the deed had been created later on and in order to show that it was an old document some mechanism like burning and use of hot vapour was applied upon the document. But such finding of the lower Courts that the deed was forged was not controverted by the High Court Division, which thereby erroneously reversed the concurrent findings of the Courts below. The learned Counsel further submits that both the Courts below found Exts. 1, 2, 3 and 4 to be genuine which demonstrated the plaintiff’s title and possession of the suit land, but the High Court Division erroneously did not consider these exhibits. He next submits that the High Court Division failed to consider the observation of the appellate Court that the trial Court had noted the forgery made by the defendant in the register of the suit R.S. khatian in connivance with the collectorate staff, but the defendant did not challenge that finding in his appeal. The learned Counsel finally submits that the High Court Division did not properly consider the oral evidence concerning the death of Brindaban Goswami and thereby came to an erroneous finding that the deed of the plaintiff was created after the death of Brindaban Goswami and was not therefore genuine.
